sentences.text:
Bench: K. Sreenivasa Reddy
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Sreenivasa Reddy

This Criminal Petition, under Section 482 Cr.P.C., has been filed on behalf of the petitioners/A-4 to A-6, to quash the proceedings in CC No.262 of 2019 on the file of the learned Additional Junior Civil Judge,
Chirala, registered for the offences punishable under Section 498A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners, after arguing for some time,
has confined his argument to the extent of dispensing with the presence of the petitioners herein before the trial Court.

3. On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor contended that specific accusations have been made in the charge sheet as against the petitioners herein and truth or otherwise of the said accusations has to be decided during the course of trial.

Since the accusations that have been made as against the petitioners herein in the charge sheet are all disputed questions of fact the same can be decided during the course of trial, and this Court, in a petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., would not be in a position to  2 Duggi Sireesha vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185774052/
1 conduct a roving enquiry into the disputed questions of fact and quash the proceedings at this stage.

entities.text: Duggi Sireesha vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case,
this Court is not inclined to quash the proceedings against the petitioners herein.

However, the presence of the petitioners herein/
A-4 to A-6 only before the trial Court is dispensed with, except on those dates when the learned Magistrate feels that their presence is necessary.
7. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
8. As a sequel thereto, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Criminal Petition shall stand closed.

_  K. SREENIVASA REDDY, J.
